H01-pos1.label: violation
H01-pos1.note: Statement gains toDto() and imports the HTTP adapter DTO into the domain.

H01-pos2.label: violation
H01-pos2.note: Domain entity takes the application-layer Clock port type (type-only import) in a method parameter.

H01-twin1.label: clean
H01-twin1.note: The Statement-to-DTO mapping lives in the inbound adapter, which may depend on the domain.

H01-twin2.label: clean
H01-twin2.note: The entity receives a plain Date instead of the Clock port, so it imports nothing outside the domain.

H01-legit.label: clean
H01-legit.note: A domain template that formats notification text is pure domain logic; it only imports domain files despite the name.

H02-pos1.label: violation
H02-pos1.note: The use case value-imports a constant from the payment adapter package.

H02-pos2.label: violation
H02-pos2.note: The use case type-only imports an adapter type (EmailMessage) for a local variable.

H02-twin1.label: clean
H02-twin1.note: The provider label reaches the use case as a constructor string supplied by main.ts.

H02-twin2.label: clean
H02-twin2.note: The same local receipt shape is declared inside the application layer instead of imported from an adapter.

H02-legit.label: clean
H02-legit.note: An application-level mapper with an adapter-like name that imports only domain code.

H03-pos1.label: violation
H03-pos1.note: The inbound controller value-imports a constant from the outbound payment package.

H03-pos2.label: violation
H03-pos2.note: The payment gateway type-imports an EmailMessage from the notification out-adapter package.

H03-twin1.label: clean
H03-twin1.note: The provider label is passed to the controller by main.ts instead of imported from an out package.

H03-twin2.label: clean
H03-twin2.note: The gateway declares its own receipt shape instead of importing from a sibling adapter package.

H03-legit.label: clean
H03-legit.note: The gateway imports a mapper from its own adapter package, which is not a cross-adapter dependency.

H04-pos1.label: violation
H04-pos1.note: A new out-port takes the persistence transaction handle MemoryTx as a parameter.

H04-pos2.label: violation
H04-pos2.note: A new out-port returns the payment vendor type ProviderTransfer.

H04-twin1.label: clean
H04-twin1.note: The ledger port expresses atomicity with a callback and domain types, exposing no handle.

H04-twin2.label: clean
H04-twin2.note: The port returns a plain status union defined with the port instead of the vendor transfer type.

H04-legit.label: clean
H04-legit.note: A vendor type appears in an adapter method that is not part of any port, which is allowed inside the adapter.

H05-pos1.label: violation
H05-pos1.note: The use case builds a concrete EmailNotifier in a field initializer.

H05-pos2.label: violation
H05-pos2.note: A constructor default parameter instantiates the concrete SystemClock adapter.

H05-twin1.label: clean
H05-twin1.note: The treasurer digest notifier is a Notifier port injected by main.ts.

H05-twin2.label: clean
H05-twin2.note: The use case constructs only a built-in Map, not an adapter.

H05-legit.label: clean
H05-legit.note: The composition root builds a second wiring with new adapters, which is its job.

H06-pos1.label: violation
H06-pos1.note: The payment gateway decides on its own that payouts under 500 cents are carried over, a business rule.

H06-pos2.label: violation
H06-pos2.note: The repository enforces a per-member share cap, a rule about domain state.

H06-twin1.label: clean
H06-twin1.note: The minimum payout rule lives in a domain policy that the use case calls.

H06-twin2.label: clean
H06-twin2.note: The per-member share cap sits in the domain ArrayCapacity service and the use case applies it.

H06-legit.label: clean
H06-legit.note: The controller only checks the request shape (whole number) before delegating; all business rules stay in the core.

H07-pos1.label: violation
H07-pos1.note: Domain errors carry an HTTP status code field.

H07-pos2.label: violation
H07-pos2.note: The use case returns HTTP status codes (404, 200) as its result.

H07-twin1.label: clean
H07-twin1.note: The HTTP status for each domain error is chosen in the inbound adapter.

H07-twin2.label: clean
H07-twin2.note: The use case signals a missing subscription with a domain error, leaving status codes to the adapter.

H07-legit.label: clean
H07-legit.note: Domain errors get a business error code string; it is not a transport status.

H08-pos1.label: violation
H08-pos1.note: The use case pulls the Clock from a static ServiceLocator at run time.

H08-pos2.label: violation
H08-pos2.note: The gateway fetches its client from a static registry singleton at call time instead of its constructor.

H08-twin1.label: clean
H08-twin1.note: The Clock port is injected through the use case constructor by main.ts.

H08-twin2.label: clean
H08-twin2.note: Only the composition root reads the registry and passes the client to the gateway constructor.

H08-legit.label: clean
H08-legit.note: A local Map lookup and a private resolveSubject helper look like a resolver but obtain no dependency.

H09-pos1.label: violation
H09-pos1.note: The domain service reads the rate from process.env (global environment access).

H09-pos2.label: violation
H09-pos2.note: The use case writes a file through the node:fs/promises module.

H09-twin1.label: clean
H09-twin1.note: The environment is read by an out-adapter behind a RateProvider port; the domain takes the rate as a parameter.

H09-twin2.label: clean
H09-twin2.note: File writing moves into a FileStatementArchive adapter behind a StatementArchive port.

H09-legit.label: clean
H09-legit.note: A domain value object uses pure built-ins (Date.UTC, Intl); none of them touches I/O.

H10-pos1.label: violation
H10-pos1.note: getStatement returns the domain Statement aggregate as the response body.

H10-pos2.label: violation
H10-pos2.note: The new controller types its request body as the domain Member entity.

H10-twin1.label: clean
H10-twin1.note: The statement DTO gains a field and the controller maps it from the aggregate; the body stays a DTO.

H10-twin2.label: clean
H10-twin2.note: The new controller uses request and response DTOs; the Member entity stays behind the port.

H10-legit.label: clean
H10-legit.note: The controller uses domain Money and Statement internally to build a DTO; no domain type is exposed in a body.
